searchText: Hi everyone! I'm trying to learn about the engine API. I think sequence diagrams would be a great tool to understand it better. I found this article: https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/consensus_api_design_space It has some diagrams like the ones I'm looking for, but it's quite outdated. Does anybody know if there are any up to date sequence diagrams for the engine API? (This is the kind of diagram I'm referring to) I have these diagrams in my ToDo list and happy to collaborate on making them happen, here is the post with a relevant and more up-to-date information https://notes.ethereum.org/DaWh-02HQ4qftum1xdphkg, it just might not describe all possible sequences I know <@290199767961567243> worked on engine api 🙂 I am not aware of any other documents describing these sequences. If you find anything, please share and if you have any particular question, please, ask -- I will try to answer it https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/233ede59d16cb01bdd8e7ff662a153a4c3178bdd/specs/overview.md#engine-api https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/233ede59d16cb01bdd8e7ff662a153a4c3178bdd/specs/exec-engine.md#engine-api Oplabs has some introductions about the engine API in applications, hoping it can bring you some help I kinda stumbled upon this fundamental question. If anyone can help me out on this, regarding Elliptic Curves in Verkle Tries Banderwagon is just a subgroup over the bandersnatch curve. Yet in all the implementation the equality check for points is different in banderwagon than that of in bandersnatch. Why? I was expecting to find some mathematical reason, or if anyone can point me to some resource Banderwagon isn't a subgroup of the Bandersnatch curve. It's actually a completely different "group" constructed as a quotient group of Bandersnatch. Internally, it uses Bandersnatch points.. but actually a Banderwagon element isn't an elliptic curve point. That's the reason why the equality check (and some other operations) are different from Bandersnatch points. Mathematically speaking, a Banderwagon element can be seen as an equivalence class between Bandersnatch points (of size 2) Probably the best resource to understand the logic for the construction is: https://hackmd.io/wliPP_RMT4emsucVuCqfHA?view Yeah have read this <@706747269424218124>, the more "down to earth" answer to the equality difference is that there're two points in Bandersnatch that map to the same Banderwagon element. If you'd use the same equality check in Bandersnatch, that couldn't solve that situation since there're two points that should be equal under "Banderwagon semantics". Okkkkk got it Now I can connect the dots. Thanks a lot for this explanantion

excerpts.author: advaitasaha
excerpts.content:
I kinda stumbled upon this fundamental question. If anyone can help me out on this, regarding Elliptic Curves in Verkle Tries

Banderwagon is just a subgroup over the bandersnatch curve. Yet in all the implementation the equality check for points is different in banderwagon than that of in bandersnatch. Why?
I was expecting to find some mathematical reason, or if anyone can point me to some resource

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
Banderwagon isn't a subgroup of the Bandersnatch curve. It's actually a completely different "group" constructed as a quotient group of Bandersnatch.
Internally, it uses Bandersnatch points.. but actually a Banderwagon element isn't an elliptic curve point. 
That's the reason why the equality check (and some other operations) are different from Bandersnatch points.

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: Mathematically speaking, a Banderwagon element can be seen as an equivalence class between Bandersnatch points (of size 2)

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: Probably the best resource to understand the logic for the construction is: https://hackmd.io/wliPP_RMT4emsucVuCqfHA?view

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
<@706747269424218124>, the more "down to earth" answer to the equality difference is that there're two points in Bandersnatch that map to the same Banderwagon element.
If you'd use the same equality check in Bandersnatch, that couldn't solve that situation since there're two points that should be equal under "Banderwagon semantics".
